newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Mobilcom sets price range for IPO.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Mobilcom sets price range for IPO.

text.p: German mobile phone group Mobilcom AG on Monday set the price range for its public share offering this month and predicted that pre-tax profits would rise more than 40 percent this year.
The initial bookbuilding phase of its share listing begins on Tuesday and ends on Thursday. Shares will be offered to investors in a range of 52.50-62.50 marks ($36.93).

MobilCom AG, which does not operate its own mobile phone network but leases capacity from other operators to repackage and resell phone services, will offer 640,000 common shares for sale to the public.

Its shares will be the first to be listed on Germany's new growth stock index, dubbed Neue Markt or new market, which is modelled after the Nasdaq index of the United States and will get off the ground on March 10.
The shares have a face value of five marks, bringing the nominal value of the entire issue to 3.2 million marks.
There is also a greenshoe, or over-allotment, of 160,000 shares, which could be issued if the offer is oversubscribed.

To promote the launch, MobilCom is promising investors a discount on their mobile telephone bill each year corresponding with the level of the MobilCom share on the day of its annual shareholders' meeting.
In addition, MobilCom customers will be able to call up a price for the DAX index and MobilCom shares on their mobile phones.
MobilCom had 1996 sales of around 309 million marks ($182.6 million) and group pre-tax profit on ordinary activities of 12.1 million marks ($7.2 million).
Mobilcom board member Carsten Meyer told reporters in Frankfurt that pre-earnings were expected to rise to 17.1 million marks this year.
Sales would rise less sharply to 314 million marks from 309 million marks and the company expected the number of subscribers to rise 50,000 to 210,000 by the end of the year.
The workforce would grow slightly to 257 employees from 222 at the end of 1996.
